text:
maya: heads-up — starting onboarding for cust Auk's LoRA (auk-lora-v1) merged onto redwood/atlas-13b. it's a multihead reparameterization, so expect different attention scaling. running quickpack now.
sam: nice. what's the target perf? latency/cost same as atlas-13b baseline?
maya: target is parity on generation quality, <=5% token-cost increase for hosted, latency SLO unchanged. main worry = int4 quant path and tokenization offsets. earlier multihead patches caused tokenmap shifts for another customer.
jin: FYI I ran a tiny smoke on int8 and int4 quantized variants — int8 looks fine, int4 shows token-prob skew on amounts and dates. quick numbers: baseline logprob mean = -1.12, auk-lora int4 = -1.35 (delta -0.23). beam-bleu / exact-match for our invoice set: baseline EM=92.1%, auk-int4 EM=88.7% (drop 3.4%).
bernie: throwing my smoke log here — ran 200 short-context prompts (invoice/amt/date) with seed=42: ```
# sample log
prompt 045: baseline -> "Total: $123.45" | auk-int4 -> "Total: $12.345" (token split)
prompt 098: baseline -> correct date 2024-02-01 | auk-int4 -> 2024-2-1 (missing zero)
aggregate: token-split anomalies 6/200, numeric-format drift 9/200
```
eval-bot: automated eval summary: quality_regression=true, primary_metric=EM_drop, value=3.4%, ll_delta=-0.23. recommended_action=run tokenizer-alignment + stitch-warmstart, run larger evalpack (2k samples) before canary.
sam: can we reproduce token split deterministically? maybe tokenizer merge ops changed when LoRA applied to query/key projection sizes. any tokenizer version mismatch between cust payload and our serving image?
maya: cust provided tokenization config pinned to v1.2. our infra default is v1.3. I did a local re-run with v1.2 and int4 drift reduced but not gone: EM went to 90.2%.
jin: ok that suggests part tokenizer + part quant numeric sensitivity. propose: 1) stitch warmstart (apply LoRA as residual, not full merge) 2) re-export with fp16 -> quantize-aware calibration using their tokenizer v1.2 3) collect attention head activations for mismatch debugging.
bernie: i can queue a canary with stitch+warmstart + v1.2 quant calibration on dedicated pool. estimated 3 hours to run full 2k evalpack. want me to go ahead?
maya: please. also add a metric to flag tokenization-stemming errors (numeric formatting normalized) and add per-token entropy delta.
eval-bot: queued job 2026-03-23T10:04Z id=auk-smoke-3311, expected finish ~3h. will post results. :robot_face:
sam: small note — if stitch reduces drift, we should document merge pattern and add to onboarding checklist (tokenizer pin, quant-calib-with-cust-toks, prefer stitch if multihead reparam).
jin: i'll draft the checklist snippet. also recommend a fallback model variant: atlas-13b-int4-safe (with conservative quant params) that runtime can route to on >2% EM regression.
maya: great. bernie, leave the canary running and ping this thread when done. I'll update the customer-facing note and request their tokenizer artifacts just in case.
bernie: starting canary now. will report back with the evalpack CSV and examples. :rocket:
